questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. Worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can make it hard to drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is safer to wait to drive than to drive when you are upset.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Create a routine for getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and check that all passengers have buckled theirs too.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar car from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all cars are the same.
Hide from your friend that you don't know the car.
Ignore any obvious problems so you don't embarrass your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn are located and how they work. Fix any problems before you drive the car.

questions.question: To stay safe when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly drive under any lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look in both directions for trains before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic must let oncoming traffic go first, even on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic must let oncoming traffic go first, even on a green light.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light to tell drivers turning left that they do not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to pass first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign tells you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: If you take over-the-counter medicine, you should:

options.text: Read the labels before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway even if there are warnings on the label.
Drive only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings, even for cold or allergy medicine. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medicine.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your car. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: T intersection.
Lane shifting.
Side road.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: T intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead and you should be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Continue to the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't try to make a last-minute turn at your exit. If you miss it, drive to the next exit instead.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and roll down your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer gets to your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel until the officer tells you what to do.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel until the officer tells you what to do.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel and make sure any passengers keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than other traffic.
Making sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. It is important to focus fully on driving. Any extra task can be dangerous.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving once you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled back in.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for the road conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of accidents. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Before you turn, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers about your plans.

questions.question: What is a passenger in a moving vehicle not allowed to do?

options.text: Have an open bottle or container of alcohol.
Sleep.
Use a cell phone.
Use a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an open bottle or container of alcohol.
questions.explanation: It is against the law to have an open alcohol container in a vehicle on a public road. The driver can face penalties for this.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal first. Then check your rear and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot. Only change lanes when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to a driver?

options.text: Reduces the ability to concentrate.
Reduces coordination.
Slows down decision-making.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait until that vehicle passes before you go.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra time for your trip.
Following speed limits.
Using turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow speed limits, and leave plenty of extra time for your trip.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the car straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
Keep your speed and drive straight.
Swerve side to side to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slowly lift your foot off the gas.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel tight and keep the car going straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control. When safe, brake gently and pull over.

questions.question: How should a seat belt fit?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Hidden under the seat.
Loose enough to turn off the warning light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable with room for your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough so you can stop within the distance you can see.
